text:
sam: rolled cniplugin v1.5.3 to prod at 08:12 UTC. after ~25% of nodes updated, we started seeing high pod-to-pod latency across GPU nodes in us-west-2a and intermittent packet loss. gpu-serving pods show timeouts on gRPC streams. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: seeing it. p95 for model-inference jumped from ~12ms to ~180ms and we have TCP retransmits in the app logs. non-gpu nodes look normal.

alex: can you paste `kubectl get pods -o wide` for a couple affected pods and an `iperf3` run between them? also which encapsulation (vxlan/geneve/underlay) did the rollout flip to?

sam: quick outputs below (from pod -> pod iperf3 run):
```
$ iperf3 -c 10.244.3.12 -t 10
[ ID]   Interval          Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  120 MBytes  100 Mbits/sec  8% packet loss  jitter 20ms
```
and kubectl shows pods on different GPU nodes (node-uw2a-gpu-03 -> node-uw2a-gpu-07).

jess: curious — our lab runs showed geneve checksumming + host jumbo frames caused fragmentation on some NIC drivers. what MTU are the hosts using vs the overlay? can you paste `ip -d link` on host?

sam: host ip link snippets:
```
2: eth0: mtu 9001 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc dd:ee:ff
3: cni0: mtu 1500 qdisc noop state DOWN mode DEFAULT group default
```
looks like host is 9001 (jumbo), overlay iface is 1500. Might be fragmentation happening.

net-bot: Alert: BGP flap detected between node-10.244.3.12 and node-10.244.7.9 — 7 occurrences in the last 10m.

maria: also found this in cniplugin logs: `ERROR endpoint: failed to allocate macvlan endpoint: timeout re-creating device` and `netlink: message too long` repeated.

alex: could be offload/segmentation or checksum offload mismatch between kernel driver and encapsulation. For RDMA-capable NICs we also saw similar issues when geneve offloads are enabled — RDMA packets get mishandled. Try disabling large-seg/offloads on the overlay iface as a quick test:
```
# on host
etctl> ethtool -K cni0 tx off rx off gro off gso off tso off
```

sam: did a tcpdump on one of the hosts, seeing lots of ICMP fragmentation-needed and some syslog `ENOBUFS` messages:
```
16:23:12.123456 IP 10.244.3.12 > 10.244.7.9: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1500
Mar 18 08:18:12 node-uw2a-gpu-07 kernel: net_dev_queue: send: dropped packet, errno -5 ENOBUFS
```

jess: OK plan: pause the rest of the rollout immediately, and rollback the nodes that haven't been updated to v1.5.2 while infra investigates MTU/driver interactions. can infra ops initiate rollback and collect `ethtool -k` and `dmesg` for the implicated nodes?

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: cniplugin-daemonset -> v1.5.2 on 18/20 targeted nodes. Job #4321 queued. :arrows_counterclockwise:

alex: action items (who/when):
- alex: run controlled iperf3 matrix with `-M` to test MSS and with fragmentation on/off in staging (30m).
- sam: collect `ethtool -k`, `ip -d link`, `dmesg | tail -n 200` from affected GPU nodes and upload to the incident folder.
- maria: correlate application retransmit logs + pod scheduling times to rollout steps.
- jess: arrange a kernel-driver test with jumbo frames and geneve offload toggled.

sam: thanks — I'm collecting logs and will attach to the rollback ticket. will post updates once rollback completes or if we see further degradation.

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: 8/18 nodes reverted, remaining 10 in progress. If rollback stalls >10m, the incident channel will be auto-notified.
